investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict", reporting that the agent quota for the eval's org has reached its hard limit of 100. Because createAgent() (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first substantive call in every remote-agents probe, the 409 caused an immediate failure before any evidence could be collected, making all three checks fail with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The failure is localized to the production-api harness reachability or routing configuration; the desktop-release sibling check passed the same contract at the same time, ruling out a shared upstream image generation service outage. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api target, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T22:57:58Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents check, none of the checks could produce any evidence, and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict", reporting that the agent quota for the eval's org has reached its hard limit of 100. Because createAgent() (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first substantive call in every remote-agents probe, the 409 caused an immediate failure before any evidence could be collected, making all three checks fail with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=1986) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint resolved by SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL was not reachable or returned an incompatible response. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=123071, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), isolating the fault to the production-api harness configuration or deployment, not to the image generation feature itself.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval probe at /api/generate/image/stream returned a 404 before the image generation session could be opened, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame and preventing any generation_completed frame or artifact URL from being produced. The failure is localized to the production-api harness reachability or routing configuration; the desktop-release sibling check passed the same contract at the same time, ruling out a shared upstream image generation service outage. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api target, not a confirmed user-facing outage.
